title: Broken Access Control
text: Enforce access control server-side on every request and deny by default. Covers missing authentication/authorization, insecure direct object references (acting on an id from the request without an ownership check), path traversal (user input reaching file paths), and open redirects to user-supplied URLs.

title: Cryptographic Failures
text: Do not use broken or weak algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, ECB mode) for security purposes, non-cryptographic random number generators for secrets or tokens, unsalted/fast hashes for passwords, plaintext transport of sensitive data, or disabled TLS certificate verification.

title: Injection
text: Untrusted input that reaches an interpreter without parameterization or proper escaping enables injection: SQL, OS command, code (eval/exec), LDAP, XPath, and cross-site scripting (user input written into HTML responses unescaped). Use parameterized APIs, argument lists, allow-lists and context-aware output encoding.

title: Insecure Design
text: Do not trust data across trust boundaries: untrusted request data must not be stored in trusted contexts such as the server-side session, and security decisions must not rely on client-controlled values (headers, hidden fields, cookies).

title: Security Misconfiguration
text: Insecure defaults and configuration: XML parsers that resolve external entities (XXE), cookies holding sensitive values without the Secure/HttpOnly flags, debug mode or verbose errors in production.

title: Identification and Authentication Failures
text: Authentication must not rely on hardcoded credentials or weak/unverified tokens; session identifiers must be protected and rotated.

title: Software and Data Integrity Failures
text: Never deserialize untrusted data with formats that can instantiate arbitrary objects (pickle, unsafe YAML loaders, marshal, jsonpickle). Verify integrity of data and code before use.

title: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
text: Logging sensitive data (credentials, card numbers, tokens) in plaintext is itself a logging failure and a data-exposure risk; unsanitized user input in logs enables log injection.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery
text: Requests to URLs built from user input let attackers reach internal services. Validate destinations against an allow-list.
